text:
HTTPS is the first line of defense in web development. It encrypts data between the user's browser and the server, preventing attackers from intercepting sensitive information like passwords or credit card numbers.

Authentication ensures that only authorized users can access certain parts of a website. Strong passwords, multi-factor authentication, and session management are all essential to verify identity safely.

Input validation is equally critical. Never trust user input. By checking and sanitizing data on the server side, developers can block common vulnerabilities such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). These attacks occur when malicious code is inserted into forms or URLs.

Ignoring these basics leaves websites exposed. A single flaw can compromise user data, damage trust, and lead to serious legal consequences. Therefore, security must be a priority from the very beginning of every project.
